author: @jeremyfowers

evidence.api_compatibility: No user-facing API changes. The only user-visible surface is the new prerelease on GitHub under candidate-v<version> tags. Stable v* release behavior is unchanged.
evidence.documentation: The PR description references RFC #3522 as having been approved, but the spec does not exist as a GitHub issue. Release notes are auto-generated by the action. No user-facing docs were updated to mention the new candidate release channel; users discovering prereleases will only find them on the GitHub Releases page. The PPA link now correctly switches between stable and candidate channels.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The entire release-v* candidate publishing path is new and has never been exercised end-to-end. A human should trigger a release branch push and verify the prerelease appears correctly on GitHub with the candidate-v<version> tag, unsigned MSIs, proper release notes, and the SmartScreen warning note.
evidence.post_approval_commits: None. Single commit (fc2c998), approved once by superm1 at 2026-09-14T19:13:32Z, merged at 2026-09-15T14:54:23Z.
evidence.review: superm1 provided 5 inline review comments on action.yml and cpp_server_build_test_release.yml, covering PPA channel naming, manual workflow dispatch, candidate tagging design, and whether inputs should be required. The author responded to each question and the reviewer approved on 2026-09-14T19:13:32Z. Both the author (@jeremyfowers, subject area includes CI) and reviewer (@superm1, subject area includes linux packaging) have CI expertise. However, a Codex bot review flagged that the release job does not include inference tests (test-exe-inference, test-deb-inference, test-watchdog-lifecycle-linux, test-dmg-inference) in its needs list, meaning a candidate could be published while inference tests are still running or after they have failed. Neither the reviewer nor the author addressed this concern.
evidence.security: Workflow uses GitHub_TOKEN for API calls (git ref creation, release publishing). Signed MSIs are downloaded for stable releases and unsigned MSIs for candidates. Release notes correctly warn that candidate installers are not signed and will trigger SmartScreen. No credentials or secrets handling concerns identified beyond standard workflow token scoping.
evidence.tests: No traditional unit tests for a CI/CD workflow change. All CI checks passed: C++ Server Build/Test/Release (conclusion: success), Validate New llama.cpp Release (success), Validate New stable-diffusion.cpp Release (success). The changes are workflow files only -- no runtime code.

maintainer_todos.text: Push a new commit to a release-v* branch and confirm the "Create GitHub Release" job publishes a prerelease under a candidate-v<version> tag with the expected artifacts and the "Windows installers are not signed" note in the release body.

subject: ci: publish release branch builds as GitHub prereleases (#3579)
summary: Adds a prerelease artifacts channel so Windows, Fedora, Debian, and macOS users can try release candidates by publishing builds from release-v* branches as GitHub prereleases under candidate-v<version> tags.
verdict_reason: All CI checks passed and the review was substantive, but a Codex bot flagged that the release job does not gate on inference tests -- a real risk that a candidate could be published before inference validation completes -- and the new candidate release path has never been exercised end-to-end by a human.
